narrative:
The model estimates a 67% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that stood out compared to employees the system expects to stay.

The strongest influence came from the fact that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal that often leads people to eventually depart, and in your case it pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving.

Next, your relatively short overall career experience of 1-5 years worked in the opposite direction. Most employees the model predicts will stay also have limited experience, so this actually helped reduce the likelihood of leaving. However, its positive effect was not enough to outweigh the other signals.

The third important factor was your employment in the “other” sector. This category shows noticeably higher turnover than fields like medicine or education, and it contributed additional push toward the prediction that you may leave.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and working in a higher-turnover sector created enough concern that the system could not confidently recommend you for promotion. 

Your organization should discuss retention strategies with you, especially around career growth and new opportunities. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals.
